A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original satellite-image retrieval, knowledge-distillation, sampling, and concept-scale experiments on Sentinel-2/NAIP and Sentinel-2/NICFI.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds correlation measurements, additional LLM results, budget evaluations, and super-resolution comparisons.

M1.justification: The LLM-based resolution choice, HR-to-LR distillation objective, disagreement-based acquisition, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.6 is rewritten without changing the algorithm; super-resolution is evaluated as an alternative rather than incorporated into the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Sentinel-2/NAIP and Sentinel-2/NICFI benchmarks, geographical coverage, retrieval task, and 40-concept vocabulary. The added experiments vary budgets and model configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–4 is unchanged. v2 Table 7 adds GRAFT LR + SR + LLM and GRAFT KD + SR + LLM, which use the HR model on super-resolution imagery to compute acquisition scores.

E3.justification: v2 adds full-system evaluations at budgets of 100, 500, and 750 locations alongside the existing 1000-location setting, tests multiple LLM backends, and introduces SR preprocessing for the new comparison. Existing dataset splits, class allocation, retrieval metrics, batch size, hardware, and default budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens component validation through quantitative HR/KD disagreement agreement on both benchmarks, checks across three LLMs, and an SR replacement analysis. Appendix A.4 also adds full-system mAP and runtime sensitivity to budget, extending the precision-versus-budget plots already present in v1.

E5.justification: Section 4.2.3 newly reports statistical correlation estimates for HR/LR versus KD/LR disagreement: 0.9322 for NAIP and 0.998 for NICFI. The existing 1000-bootstrap-sample analysis and 90% confidence-interval statement remain unchanged; no additional seed counts or uncertainty intervals are reported.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–4 and the per-concept results are unchanged, but v2 adds substantive findings on disagreement correlations, smaller-budget performance, and SR accuracy/runtime tradeoffs. Table 7 reports unseen-class mAP@100/mAP@20 of 0.556/0.589 for KD + SR + LLM at 12,884 seconds, versus the retained full-system values of 0.502/0.564 at 372 seconds. Table 5 expands one generic LLM row to three named models, each reporting 100% accuracy.

T1.justification: The problem assumptions and Equations 1–5, including HR score aggregation, the distillation loss, and disagreement definitions, are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central budget-aware recognition claims. The headline claims of up to 26.3% improvement and 76.3% fewer HR images are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 adds an explanation contrasting task-focused distillation with SR reconstruction of high-frequency details and interprets the resulting accuracy/runtime tradeoff. Section 4.2.4 adds stronger language about extending LLM selection to more concepts. Existing limitations concerning discrete resolutions, OSM noise, and segmentation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 identifies ChatGPT 3.5, Gemini, and Claude and documents the SR pipeline: 32×32 patches from 256×256 images, 320,960 patch evaluations, stitching and subdivision, and 12,549.90 seconds for SR generation. These details were absent from v1, although the exact SR model and Gemini/Claude versions remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The same 50 cited works and related-work subsections are retained; author-year citations are formatting changes. Appendix A.5 adds an efficiency-based distinction from super-resolution, extending v1's discussion of SR hallucination with arguments about computational cost and task relevance.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. v2 rewrites Sections 3.6 and 4.2.4, changes 'Detection in Low Resolution' to 'Recognition in Low Resolution,' adds appendix subsections and cross-references, and replaces citation placeholders with author-year references.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 5 and adds Tables 6–7; the original per-concept Table 6 becomes unchanged Table 8. All four figures retain their graphical content, with resizing, a revised Figure 3 caption, and relocation of Figure 4. Title, heading, and running-header styles also change.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the empirical support through quantitative disagreement agreement, full-system budget tradeoffs, and a direct SR comparison that exposes improved unseen-class accuracy at roughly 34 times the runtime. These are useful additions to otherwise unchanged core results. The unnamed SR model and the unchanged ten-unseen-concept evaluation limit reproducibility and support for the broader generalizations.
